newsitem.title: USA: U.S. investigating envoy to Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investigating envoy to Saudi Arabia.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said on Friday it was investigating reports that its ambassador to Saudi Arabia may have improperly shared information about U.S. diplomatic discussions with Saudi officials.
The issue was raised on Friday in the Washington Post quoting a letter the newspaper said it obtained from the Glasgow Evening Times and was authenticated by the State Department.
The letter was written by the ambassador, former Georgia Sen. Wyche Fowler, 55, who is married, to 24-year-old Scottish physiotherapist and sports shop manager Josephine Morton.

"We're talking to Ambassador Fowler. We're looking into, you know, the issue that was raised in the Al Kamen (Washington Post) column," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters. Kamen writes a political gossip column.
Burns refused to discuss the letter in detail.

But the newspaper quoted Fowler as writing on embassy stationery on Oct. 8: "I've been working hard meeting influential Saudis, including the King, Crown prince and his cabinet ... Soon I must visit when I have no agenda -- such as asking permission to launch strikes against other Islamic nations from Saudi territory."
The Saudis refused the use of their territory for U.S. strikes at Iraq a month earlier.
The State Department tells reporters regularly that as a matter of policy it will not divulge its discussions with foreign governments.
